messages:
tara: Heads-up — small but noisy reconnect/double-bill spike on ws route 'user-stream' in us-west around 09:12 UTC. console shows lots of short sockets and billing events. anyone oncall?

ben: i noticed it. pattern: client gets a CLOSE 1006 then immediately reopens; proxy logs a 204 at same time. feels like a canary change to resume_ttl landed early this morning.

eli: timeline w/ logs: ```
[09:12:10] proxy: route=user-stream status=204 conn=786 closed_upstream close_code=1006 resume_ttl=0ms
[09:12:10] client-sdk: reconnect attempt=1 backoff=0s
[09:12:11] billing: emit session.create id=evt_542 token=tok_abc route=user-stream
```

meera: resume_ttl=0ms again. that makes 204 mean 'session tombstoned' and clients re-create immediately -> billing storm.

tara: infra-bot: can you verify session.create delta and how many unique tokens had >1 create?

infra-bot: [automated] streaming.session.create for route "user-stream" increased 2.9x between 09:10 and 09:15 UTC. unique tokens with >1 create: 38 -> 172.

ben: mitigation options: 1) revert resume_ttl change in canary (quick, low risk) 2) server-side: treat 204 returned after abrupt close (1006) as soft-close and debounce session create for 300ms 3) billing dedupe by accepting idempotency header on session.create 4) client change: jittered backoff for CLOSE/204.

eli: prefer server-side guard first — many customers run older SDKs. also need console: annotate reconnect chart with recent flag toggles so SREs can correlate quickly.

meera: agree. raise one nuance: we should differentiate TCP/1006 early-close vs graceful 1000 close. if graceful 1000 + 204 probably safe to recreate, if 1006 treat as transient. server debounce should check close_code.

ben: good call. console-bot: can we add an overlay for recent feature flag flips on the reconnect graph and a heatmap for per-token reconnects?

console-bot: [automated] UX request captured: reconnect-flag-overlay + per-token heatmap. ticket CON-4001 created.

billing-bot: [automated] billing service can dedupe session.create using X-Session-Id within a 2s window behind flag BILLING-DEDUPE-2S.

eli: i'll open a small PR that implements server-side soft-204 debounce when close_code != 1000 plus unit/integration tests that simulate 1006+204 -> immediate reconnect loop. will tag meera.

tara: ops: i've started rollback of resume_ttl change to canary now.

infra-bot: [automated] rollback performed at 09:18 UTC. session.create rate back to 1.05x baseline by 09:23 UTC.

meera: follow-ups & owners: - server debounce implementation & tests (eli) - billing idempotency toggle + e2e (niranjan) - console overlay + heatmap (josh/console) - client SDK note about backoff (devex) - alert: reconnect_rate > baseline*2 AND recent_flag_change < 15m -> page (meera).

ben: small doc ask: add a snippet in streaming quickstart about handling CLOSE 1006 vs 1000 and recommending exponential backoff for immediate reconnects.

eli: PR #9120 created: "server: debounce soft-204 on abrupt close (1006) 300ms + test". description: avoids rapid session re-create storms when resume_ttl is tiny.

meera: thanks all. scheduling a 20m blameless postmortem to capture rollout guardrails. closing thread when POAPs created. :white_check_mark:
